llm.summary: This image-generation skill is coherent and disclosed, but it sends prompts and selected media to dLazy and can store an API key locally.

dimensions.detail: Network use and uploads are disclosed: prompts and parameters go to api.dlazy.com, selected local media paths are uploaded to files.dlazy.com, and generated assets are hosted there, which is proportionate for a cloud image-generation API.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses a pinned third-party npm/npx dependency, @dlazy/cli@1.2.3, with an optional global install; npm package metadata and tarball inspection did not show install-time scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent instructions are scoped to running dlazy banana2 and reporting authentication or credit errors, but the English and Chinese trigger keywords include broad generic image-generation phrases that could benefit from explicit user intent before invocation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI can persist a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json after login or auth set; this is disclosed, user-scoped, and described as revocable, with no background worker or unrelated persistence found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Nano Banana 2.0 image generation/editing through the dLazy CLI, and the documented banana2 command, prompt/image options, output format, and error handling all match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using dLazy as a third-party cloud image service. Confirm before sending private prompts or local media, prefer npx or the documented pinned version if you do not want a persistent global binary, and revoke or rotate the dLazy API key if you stop using it.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The English generic trigger phrases are broad, but they describe the advertised image-generation/editing purpose; this is a user-control caution rather than evidence of hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese generic trigger phrases carry the same overbreadth concern, but the artifact clearly discloses the third-party API, uploads, authentication, and local API-key storage.
